title: A unified stochastic random walk theory for Kolmogorov spectrum, halo mass functions, and halo density profiles
authors: Zhijie Xu
abstract: We develop a unified stochastic framework for nonequilibrium systems and apply it to turbulence and cosmic structure formation. Spectra and distributions evolve by transport in "scale space", described by random walks and Fokker-Planck equations with scale-dependent waiting times. We reformulate the turbulent cascade as a random walk in wavenumber space with waiting time $\tau_{gk}\propto k^{-\gamma}$. With $\gamma=2/3$ fixed by self-consistency, we recover the Kolmogorov $-5/3$ law and obtain the full energy spectrum, including the inertial-dissipation crossover, exponential cutoff and spectrum constant, without applying dimensional analysis to the spectrum itself. In bottom-up hierarchical structure formation, low-mass haloes collapse early and retain primordial imprints, while prolonged assembly near the characteristic mass $m_h^*$ erases this memory and establishes a universal spectrum $P(k)\propto k^{-1}$. We model this as a random walk in halo mass space with $\tau_g\propto m_h^{-\lambda}$. This yields a stretched Gaussian halo mass function that reproduces the Press-Schechter form, with small-scale scaling $f_M\propto m_h^{-\lambda}$ and an exponential cutoff at $m_h>m_h^*$, both set by $\lambda$. It also produces a double-$\lambda$ mass function: $\lambda$ reflects the primordial spectrum at low masses and approaches $2/3$ near $m_h^*$, where gravity dominates. For individual haloes, a spatial random walk with $\tau_{gr}\propto r^{-\gamma}$ generates a double-$\gamma$ density profile that reproduces the Einasto profile, with small-scale scaling $\rho_r\propto r^{-2\gamma}$ and an exponential cutoff at $r>r_s$, both set by $\gamma$. Here $\gamma$ is fixed by the initial spectrum in the inner core and approaches $2/3$ ($\rho_r\propto r^{-4/3}$) in the gravity-dominated outskirts. This framework thus describes turbulent cascades and cosmic structure formation on a common footing.
comments: 16 pages, Published at Scientific Reports

figs.cap: Schematic depiction of a random walk in wavenumber k space underlying the turbulence energy spectrum. Energy is injected at the integral scale $k_{L}$ (or equivalently $L$ in real space), represented by a delta-like distribution of a group of “energy carriers”, each carrying an infinitesimal energy $dE$. The dominant local triadic interactions (k+p+q=0) transfer "energy carriers" (blue dots) from a wavenumber k to a nearby wavenumber k+$\delta$k, producing a step-wise random walk toward larger k (red arrows). Each step conserves total energy, while the waiting time $\tau_{gk}$(k) between steps depends on k and encodes the finite lifetime of eddies at that scale. In the stationary state, the resulting distribution $P(k)$ of "energy carriers" is proportional to the energy spectrum $E(k)$, shown here as a Kolmogorov -5/3 law with an exponential cutoff near the dissipation wavenumber $k_{\eta}$ (or $\eta$ in real space), where viscous effects dominate and remove energy.

Schematic of the halo random walk in mass space. A halo of mass $M$ that accretes a free particle of mass $m$ steps to $M+m$, carrying mass toward larger halo masses. For a halo of mass $m_{h}$, such events occur after an average waiting time $\tau_{g}(m_{h})$. Starting from sharply localized initial conditions, the process generates the halo mass function as the solution of the associated Fokker–Planck equation.

Compensated density power spectrum $P(k)k$ for IllustrisTNG (Springel et al., 2018) and Illustris-1-Dark (Vogelsberger et al., 2014) at $z=0,\,1,\,3$, with the linear prediction. A horizontal plateau indicates $n=-1$, i.e. $P(k)\propto k^{-1}$, as expected for gravity-dominated dynamics. The plateau on 1–10 Mpc scales (dashed lines) widens toward lower redshift as nonlinear collapse advances; on sub-Mpc scales the spectrum declines, retaining the primordial imprint.

Evolution of two mass scales, $M^{*}(a)$ and $m_{h}^{*}(a)$, in the Virgo SCDM (Jenkins et al., 1998) and Illustris-1-Dark (Vogelsberger et al., 2014) simulations. In Illustris-1-Dark, $m_{h}^{*}\propto a^{3}$ ($M^{*}\propto a^{15/4}$) before the crossover $a_{*}$ and $m_{h}^{*}\propto a^{3/2}$ ($M^{*}\propto a^{3}$) at late times (dashed line).

Compensated halo density profiles $\rho_{r}(r)r^{4/3}$ for six sets of high-resolution $N$-body simulations: (1) Ghalo (Stadel et al., 2009); (2) Via Lactea (Diemand et al., 2008); (3) Aquarius (Springel et al., 2008); (4) Dubinski (Dubinski and Carlberg, 1991); (5) FIRE:DMO (McKeown et al., 2022); (6) Illustris-1-Dark (Vogelsberger et al., 2014). Multiplying by $r^{4/3}$ removes the $-4/3$ slope, so a horizontal plateau in this representation indicates a density profile consistent with $\rho_{r}\propto r^{-4/3}$ (Eq. (50)) dominated by gravitational dynamics. Most simulated haloes of $10^{12}M_{sun}$ show an approximately flat plateau on scales of several kpc (between the two dashed lines), whose extent grows with halo mass. On sub-kpc scales, the compensated profile declines at small $r$, indicating a shallower inner slope that is sensitive to the primordial spectrum.

Logarithmic density slope $s=d\ln\rho_{r}/d\ln r$ as a function of radius $r$, shown for five simulated dark matter haloes with masses around $10^{12}\,M_{\odot}$: Aquarius (Springel et al., 2008), VL2 and Ghalo$_{3}$ (Stadel et al., 2009), Via Lactea (Diemand et al., 2008), and FIRE:DMO (McKeown et al., 2022). Three regimes are marked: a primordial-spectrum-dominated regime at small $r$, a gravity-dominated regime at intermediate $r$ (between the dashed red lines), and a linear regime at large $r$. Within the gravity-dominated regime, all profiles flatten to a common slope of approximately $s\approx-4/3$ (dashed black line) over the scale range $r\sim 1$ to 6 kpc, reflecting a universal density scaling once gravitational collapse dominates.

title: Clumping Factor in the Mix: Incomplete Mixing Suppresses Turbulent Reaction Boost
authors: Yu-hsuan Liu, Chia-Yu Hu
abstract: Cosmological simulations often account for unresolved density fluctuations using a sub-grid clumping factor when modeling chemical reactions. To validate this approach, we conduct hydrodynamical simulations of isothermal, supersonic turbulence and track the evolution of passive chemical species in first-, second-, and third-order reactions, exploring seven reaction rates across Mach numbers $M$ = 2-50 in three turbulence driving modes. We parametrize the saturation of clumping factors at $M \gtrsim 10$ due to intermittency (i.e., falling significantly below the log-normal prediction) with a one-parameter fitting formula. Furthermore, we find that the competition between turbulent mixing and the density-dependent reaction rates, governed by the Damköhler number (Da), suppresses the global reaction rate by a \textit{mixing efficiency} factor ($\xi$). For Da $\ll 1$, chemical species remain well mixed ($\xi\to 1$), and the reaction rates are boosted by a clumping factor. For Da $\gg 1$, reactants in dense gas are rapidly depleted before being redistributed by turbulence, causing $\xi$ to drop by a factor of a few to more than an order of magnitude. We quantify the effective mixing efficiency as a function of two dimensionless parameters, $M$ and Da, and provide a fitting formula that can be easily adopted in cosmological simulations to accurately follow unresolved chemical reactions.
comments: 16 pages, 10 figures, submitted; comments welcome

title: Tentative Excess Dispersion Measures toward DESI Galaxy Groups from Localized Fast Radio Bursts
authors: Jiale Wang, Taotao Fang
abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide sensitive probes of ionized baryons through their dispersion measures (DMs). In this work, we test whether localized FRB sight lines intersecting foreground galaxy groups exhibit a measurable excess in cosmic DM relative to clean nonintersecting sight lines. We crossmatch 117 localized FRBs with measured DMs and host redshifts against a foreground group catalog from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Within the catalog footprint and at $z_{\rm host}<0.5$, we identify 23 sight lines intersecting foreground groups and 18 clean nonintersecting sight lines for the main comparison. A joint fit to this sample gives a positive offset of $143.3^{+53.2}_{-53.0}~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ in the inferred cosmic DM, $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cosmic}$, for the group-intersecting sight lines relative to the nonintersecting control sample. A template fit for the foreground halos gives $A_{\rm halo}=0.34^{+0.51}_{-0.50}$, with a positive posterior median but a weakly constrained detailed halo contribution. A mock forecast within the DESI footprint indicates that larger samples of localized FRBs would improve the foreground halo template constraint.

title: Elastic polar oscillations and nuclear parameters
authors: Hajime Sotani
abstract: Owing to the elasticity of a neutron star, the shear and interface modes are excited, in addition to the fundamental, pressure, and gravity modes. While direct observations of the oscillation spectrum remain challenging, potential resonance signatures from these modes could be manifested in the precursors of short gamma-ray bursts from binary neutron star mergers. If the oscillation spectrum is observed, this is a good opportunity to extract the physical properties through the technique of asteroseismology. In particular, we focus on the crustal elasticity and examine the $s$- and $i$-mode frequencies. We find that, for a given EOS specified by the nuclear saturation parameters, the radius-scaled $s$-mode frequencies and the mass-scaled $i$-mode frequencies can be expressed as a function of the stellar compactness, independently of the stiffness of the core EOS, at least when the EOS in a higher-density region can be characterized only by the specific constant sound velocity. Then, we could derive the fitting formula for the $s_i$-mode for $i=1-4$ and $i_1$-mode frequencies as a function of the stellar compactness and the combination of the incompressibility of symmetric nuclear matter, $K_0$, and the slope parameter for the nuclear symmetry energy, $L$. If the $s$- and/or $i$-mode oscillation frequencies were observed, one may get the relation between these properties by identifying the observed frequencies with specific modes, using our fitting formula, which offers useful insights into the nuclear saturation parameters and stellar properties. By combining the other observational data, it may be possible to narrow the parameter space of EOS parameters and stellar properties. We emphasize that this article summarizes the results presented in our previous studies and discusses their implications for neutron star seismology.

title: Phase-Resolved X-ray Polarimetry of LMC X-1: Enhanced Polarization at Inferior Conjunction
authors: Yu-Shan Ling, Fei Xie, Alessandro Di Marco, Fabio La Monaca
abstract: We present a phase-resolved X-ray polarimetric analysis of the extragalactic black hole X-ray binary LMC X-1, a classical high/soft state source with a well-characterized accretion disk and an ionization cone/inferred jet. Previous X-ray polarimetry gave only orbit-averaged upper limits on the polarization fraction, leaving any orbital-phase dependence unexplored. We aim to probe how this polarization depends on orbital phase and to identify the origin of the polarized emission. We analyzed simultaneous IXPE, NICER, and NuSTAR observations taken in October 2022. We measured the polarization degree and angle in different energy bands as a function of orbital phase, performed spectro-polarimetric modeling to identify the emitting components, and modeled the phase modulation of the Stokes parameters with a cosine function. The polarization depends on orbital phase: during inferior conjunction (phase from -0.1 to 0.1), the polarization degree is (4.2+/-1.1)% in 2-3 keV and (3.4+/-0.8)% in 2-8 keV, with polarization angles of (46+/-8) and (50+/-7) degrees. Outside this phase it stays below the 99% minimum detectable polarization. The measured angle agrees with the ionization cone/jet direction (~45 degrees), and spectro-polarimetric modeling favors a soft-band origin for the polarization. The Stokes Q/I and U/I modulation is well described by a cosine at the orbital period and favors two spatially separated polarized components over a single one varying in amplitude. We also tested whether differential Faraday rotation of the disk light in an ordered magnetic field can reproduce the modulation and used it to place upper limits on the magnetic field. These results show that soft-band polarization of LMC X-1 appears only near inferior conjunction at a position angle aligned with the disk normal, and highlight the importance of orbital-phase sampling in polarimetric studies.

title: A dedicated survey of fast-rotating near-Earth asteroids with the Two-meter Twin Telescope. II. Tumblers
authors: M. R. Alarcon, D.J. Scheeres, J. Licandro, C.J. Benson, M. Serra-Ricart
abstract: Fast rotation dominates the metre- to decametre-size near-Earth asteroid (NEA) population, but the incidence of non-principal-axis (NPA) rotation, or tumbling, in this regime is essentially unconstrained. We establish how common NPA rotation is among small, fast-rotating NEAs, how its prevalence varies with size, and what it implies for the internal structure and recent dynamical history of these bodies. We analysed the homogeneous high-cadence sample obtained with the Two-meter Twin Telescope at Teide Observatory and presented in the first paper of this series. Light curves showing coherent residual structure under a single-frequency Fourier model were refitted with a bivariate Fourier series in two independent frequencies, and dynamical modes were assigned from the normalised harmonic amplitude spectrum. We confirm 32 NPA rotators, 14 with both periods reliably resolved, with periods spanning 0.48-46.4 min and estimated diameters of 7-140 m. The most extreme object with both periods resolved, 2025 FB8 (shortest period $P_1 = 71$ s, estimated diameter $D \simeq 7$ m), is the fastest and smallest such tumbler characterised to date. Eight objects satisfy our harmonic quality criteria, and all eight are consistent with long-axis mode rotation. The tumbler fraction among fast rotators is 16.0 %, rising from 13.8 % at absolute magnitude $H < 26$ to 22.5 % at $H \geq 26$. Twenty-three of the 32 lie above the spin limit of a cohesionless rubble pile; none exceeds the lunar-regolith limit. Tumbling is common among small fast rotators, with no evidence that it becomes rarer towards the smallest sizes. Fast tumblers require modest cohesion but no monolithic interior, occupying the same structural domain as their principal-axis counterparts.
comments: Accepted for publication in A&A. 10 pages, 3 figures

In both cases the body axis $\boldsymbol{c}$ precesses around the fixed angular momentum vector $\boldsymbol{L}$ with angular velocity $\omega_{\phi}$, while the body rotates about $\boldsymbol{c}$ with angular velocity $\omega_{\psi}$. In LAM (left), $\boldsymbol{c}$ is the longest principal axis of the body; in SAM (right), $\boldsymbol{c}$ is the shortest principal axis. The figure shows that the same two-component motion—precession and rotation—gives rise to qualitatively different orientations of the body with respect to $\boldsymbol{L}$ in each mode.

title: The Eclipsing $γ$ Doradus Star VZ Canum Venaticorum
authors: Jae Woo Lee
abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the eclipsing binary VZ CVn using TESS Sectors 50 and 77 photometry together with published spectroscopic results. The TESS light curves were modeled to refine the binary parameters, and the residual light curves were analyzed to investigate the pulsational properties of the system. We derive masses and radii of $M_{\rm A}=1.526\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm A}=1.638\pm0.023$ $R_\odot$ for the primary and $M_{\rm B}=1.259\pm0.005$ $M_\odot$ and $R_{\rm B}=1.133\pm0.016$ $R_\odot$ for the secondary. Comparison with PARSEC evolutionary models suggests a near-solar metallicity of $Z=0.017$ and an age of 1.0 Gyr. Separate frequency analyses of the two TESS sectors reveal four signals with possible counterparts in both sectors. Two of these frequencies, $f_2=4.7486$ day$^{-1}$ and $f_6=7.1242$ day$^{-1}$, are consistent with the fourth and sixth orbital harmonics, respectively, suggesting an orbital origin rather than independent $\delta$ Sct pulsations. The dominant frequency $f_1=1.7577$ day$^{-1}$ has a pulsation constant of $Q_1=0.336$ day, consistent with a $\gamma$ Dor-type g-mode pulsation. The weaker signal $f_5=1.9754$ day$^{-1}$ also has a pulsation constant of $Q_5=0.299$ day, although its detection remains tentative because of its low S/N. Together with the physical and evolutionary properties of the primary, these results support its classification as a $\gamma$ Dor pulsator rather than the previously proposed $\gamma$ Dor--$\delta$ Sct hybrid pulsator.
comments: 9 pages, including 4 figures and 3 tables, accepted for publication in PASJ

title: A Wideband Technosignature Search of 210,191 Nearby Main-sequence Stars with the VLA Sky Survey
authors: Steve Croft
abstract: Searches for radio technosignatures have concentrated on narrowband signals. We present a complementary search for excess broadband 2-4 GHz emission from 210,191 Gaia DR3 main-sequence stars within 100 pc in all epochs of the VLA Sky Survey (VLASS; 2017-2026). Cross-matching with the Epoch-1 catalog yields 51 high-reliability positional associations (versus 1.5 expected by chance). All but one are known natural emitters that, where measurable, move with their stars; the remaining source, near LSPM J1943+5337, is not at the star. Because stellar flares can mimic transmitters in continuum flux, a detection counts as a possible transmitter at any luminosity only at the 32,985 apparently single AFGK stars outside known radio-emitter classes, and at M dwarfs and AFGK multiples only above $10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Forced photometry of 208,232 stars in all epochs finds 1 steady-test detection and 3 stars detected in at least one epoch among the eligible stars, against 1.3 and 1.9 expected by chance. The median per-star limit on steady emission is $L_\nu<4.0\times10^{8}$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Without background subtraction, fewer than $1.5\times10^{-4}$ of eligible AFGK stars host a steady transmitter above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$, and fewer than $2.3\times10^{-5}$ of all stars outside the known-emitter classes host one above $\sim1.1\times10^{10}$ W Hz$^{-1}$; counting every M-dwarf detection as a possible transmitter, fewer than $5.5\times10^{-4}$ of M dwarfs host one above $10^9$ W Hz$^{-1}$. Stacks detect population-averaged emission from M dwarfs, concentrated in those with activity evidence. Continuum surveys thus constrain broadband, modulated, or rapidly drifting signals that narrowband pipelines do not search for.
comments: 30 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to AAS Journals

title: Quiet-Sun magnetic field configuration inferred from the ratio of longitudinal fields measured in the Fe I λ6301 and λ6302 Å lines
authors: Sergey Grigoryevich Mozharovsky
abstract: The estimate of the longitudinal magnetic field obtained from the Hinode spectropolarimeter data will be different if it is determined in different ways. In particular, the values obtained by the Center Of Gravity (COG) method for the Fe I $\lambda$ 6301 and 6302 $Å$ lines do not coincide. Some of the differences are due to the different inaccuracies of the COG method for each of the two lines. However, some of the differences can be explained by the fact that the response functions of these lines to changes in the magnetic field are formed at different heights. This should be accompanied by a certain morphological structure of magnetic fields. It consists in the fact that most of the magnetic configurations of the quiet photosphere are similar to each other. To a rough approximation, their structure can be compared with the structure of a sunspot - there is a central region with the strongest field, close to vertical, and slopes - an analog of penumbra, where the field weakens and / or turns to horizontal. This turn occurs at the heights of the greatest response of the Fe I $\lambda$ 6301 and 6302 $Å$ lines to changes in the magnetic field with a turn length of about tens of kilometers.

The diagrams (c, f) show a comparison of the values of $B_{\mathrm{IV},6301}$ and $B_{\mathrm{IV},6302}$, obtained using the COG method.

title: Thermal evolution of Uranus and Neptune, hydrogen-water phase separation and the role of methane
authors: Marina Cano Amoros, Nicola Tosi, Nadine Nettelmann
abstract: Adiabatic evolution models of Uranus and Neptune with constant compositional stratification miss their observed luminosities: Uranus is fainter than commonly predicted, while improved equations of state (EoS) have recently led to a brightness problem for Neptune. In adiabatic models of Jupiter and Saturn, helium rain is thought to enhance luminosity. In the ice giants, hydrogen-water phase separation (H2-H2O demixing) with water rain has recently been predicted. We aim to understand how H2-H2O demixing and the EoS of water influence the luminosity of Uranus and Neptune. We use state-of-the-art EoS of H, He, H2O, and the H2-H2O phase diagram to build adiabatic three-layer models of the present-day structure that match the observed gravity field and the phase diagram. We compute evolution tracks with and without demixing, and for Neptune, with and without latent heat and methane, for which we provide an updated large-scale EoS including entropy. Without demixing, adiabatic Neptune with the revised AQUA EoS, without methane or latent heat, cools to its observed luminosity within 4.5 Gyr, in good agreement with the age of the Solar system. Applying the same assumptions to Uranus would require a Bond albedo of 0.43 to explain its luminosity. With demixing, the radii expand while the luminosity decreases. For Uranus, demixing leads to an equilibrium evolution with the incident flux that naturally explains its faintness. Demixing also makes Neptune fainter. Methane reduces the radius expansion but not the faintness problem. Favored Neptune models include demixing and methane at an initial C/O ratio of $\sim$1 due to CO ice accretion, with cooling times of $\lesssim 4 Gyr. Neptune requires an additional heat source unless its structure is primordial and the outer envelope is ice-poor, while hydrogen-water phase separation is an option to explain the structure and faintness of Uranus.
comments: 12 main text and 5 appendix pages, 10 figures

title: Jupiter's Evolving Interior as a Source of Episodic Heating on Europa
authors: Jasmine Sun, Benjamin Idini, Ruth Murray-Clay
abstract: Jupiter's evolving interior can affect the orbital evolution of its moons through frequency-dependent tidal dissipation. We investigate how encounters between the Galilean satellites and Jupiter's oscillation modes affect the stability of the Laplace resonance and Europa's tidal heating. Using the N-body integrator REBOUNDx, we simulate the dynamical orbital evolution of Io, Europa, and Ganymede, with tidal migration timescales derived from three representative models of Jupiter's interior. Encounters with a Jovian tidal resonance can alter the libration state of the Laplace angle, excite orbital eccentricity, and/or destroy the Laplace resonant chain. The outcome of the satellite system depends on which moon experiences enhanced tidal migration. Resonance locks involving Io or Europa can sustain outward migration of the Laplace resonant chain, whereas Ganymede locks destroy the chain. Notably, transient resonance crossings can excite Europa's eccentricity without breaking the Laplace resonance. Under our adopted eccentricity-damping prescription, the baseline tidal power is typically of the order $10^{11}$-$10^{12}$ W, with transient episodes reaching roughly an order of magnitude higher power. These results provide a mechanism for episodic tidal heating on Europa without requiring thermal feedback within the satellites.
comments: 15 pages, 2 page appendix, 10 figures

figs.cap: Schematic illustration of tidal forcing by Io, Europa, and Ganymede on Jupiter. Because Jupiter rotates much faster than the moons orbit, its dissipative tidal response is displaced ahead of each moon-Jupiter line, exerting a forward torque that transfers angular momentum from Jupiter’s spin to the moons’ orbits. The arrows indicate the moons’ orbital frequencies $n_{i}$, which approximately follow the Laplace commensurability ($n_{i}/n_{i+1}\approx 2$). Each moon forces Jupiter at a different tidal frequency, $\omega_{f}=m(\Omega_{J}-n)$, producing a frequency-dependent dynamical tidal response.

(a) Semi-major axis evolution timescales $\tau_{a}$ produced by tidal excitation of oscillations in three representative models of Jupiter’s dilute core. Sharp features mark tidal resonances between the satellite forcing and Jupiter’s oscillation modes for a reference satellite of mass $m_{s}=10^{25}$ g. The red line shows a constant-$Q$ tidal model for comparison with $Q=10^{5}$. The dashed line shows the normal-mode evolution timescale $t_{\text{evol}}=50$ Gyr used here. (b) Models of Jupiter’s dilute core: Compact [26, 11, 51], Smooth [5], and Sharp [27, 11, 51]. Metallicity is the mass fraction of heavy elements relative to the total mass. All three models fit the same Jupiter average radius.

Projected Laplace phase-space trajectories in $(e_{\rm Eu}\cos\phi_{L},e_{\rm Eu}\sin\phi_{L})$. (a) Full $N$-body simulation showing circulation (region 1), symmetric libration about $\phi_{L}=\pi$ (region 2), and asymmetric libration (regions 3 and 4). (b) Trajectories from simplified simulations placing Io and Ganymede on circular orbits and treating Europa as a massless test particle with $e_{\rm Eu}=0.02$–$0.2$. Successive libration cycles trace nearly closed curves, except near the transition between libration states ($e_{2}=0.07$, green dotted curve). The asymmetric trajectory near $\phi_{L}=\pi/2$ with $e_{2}=0.1$ uses the initial conditions in Table 2.

Evolution of Jupiter’s tidal migration profiles for the Compact (top), Smooth (middle), and Sharp (bottom) interior models. Colors indicate the prescribed migration timescale $\tau_{a}$ as a function of semimajor axis and time; narrow minima trace the outward drift of Jovian tidal resonances. Red curves show the semimajor axes of Io, Europa, and Ganymede in representative simulations. The adopted mode-evolution timescales are $t_{\rm evol}=50$, 50, and 40 Gyr, respectively. Vertical dashed lines mark the moons’ present-day orbital distances. The orbital elements of these three simulations are in Figures 8 and 9.

First 1 Gyr of orbital evolution in the Compact core simulation (Fig. 7,top). The satellites begin just wide of the 2:1 commensurabilities, with initial adjacent mean-motion ratios of 2.01. Europa becomes locked to a Jovian tidal resonance at approximately 0.25 Gyr. Ganymede subsequently locks near 0.6 Gyr, disrupting the Laplace resonance.

Orbital evolution in representative Smooth-core (a) and Sharp-core (b) simulations. (a) Starting from exact 2:1 period ratios, Io locks to a Jovian tidal resonance near 0.4 Gyr, followed by Europa near 1 Gyr. Subsequent Io resonance crossings excite the satellite eccentricities before a Ganymede lock disrupts the Laplace resonance at approximately 4.3 Gyr. (b) Starting from period ratios of 2.02, the satellites are captured into the Laplace resonance through convergent migration. Europa locks near 0.8 Gyr, while later Io resonance crossings produce temporary eccentricity enhancements without disrupting the Laplace resonance. The rapid variations in Europa’s prescribed $\tau_{a}$ in panel (a) likely reflect the steep gradient of the narrow Jovian tidal resonance to which Europa is locked, as opposed to the wider resonance Europa is locked to in (b).

title: Nonlinear models of Mira variables with long secondary periods
authors: Yu. A. Fadeyev
abstract: Calculations of nonlinear radial oscillations in asymptotic giant branch stars with an initial mass of $M_\mathrm{ZAMS}=1.6M_\odot$ were performed for initial helium and metal abundances of $Y=0.28$ and $Z=0.006$, respectively. Several models from the evolutionary sequence after the 4th thermal pulse were used as initial conditions for the hydrodynamic equations describing stellar pulsations with long secondary periods. Using the discrete Fourier transform of the hydrodynamic solutions we show that long secondary periods appear in Mira variables pulsating simultaneously in the fundamental mode and first overtone with non-multiple periods. The relative deviation from multiplicity is $\delta_\mathrm{\Pi}\le 1.2\times 10^{-2}$ and is responsible for mode splitting into equally spaced frequency components, each of which is a standing wave with a free outer boundary. The cycle length of long secondary periods is nearly 20 times that of the fundamental mode. Long secondary periodicity is a nonlinear effect that arises after reaching the limiting amplitude and develops over several hundred fundamental mode periods.
comments: 11 pages, 6 figures, accepted to Astronomy Letters

Hydrodynamic models with decaying oscillations are shown by open circles. Models with regular oscillations and those with the LSP are marked by filled circles and asterisks, respectively.

title: Robust Measurements of the Cosmic Microwave Background Lensing Power Spectrum in the Presence of Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence
authors: Rui Zhou, Michael Doohan, Christian L. Reichardt
abstract: Achieving the scientific potential of upcoming high-sensitivity cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization surveys requires lensing analyses that are robust to unmodeled distortions of the polarization field. One such possible distortion is anisotropic cosmic birefringence, a direction-dependent rotation of the linear polarization plane that may arise from parity-violating physics such as axion-like fields. We quantify the impact of both modeled and unmodeled anisotropic birefringence on the CMB lensing measurement in the Marginal Unbiased Score Expansion (MUSE) framework. Considering noise levels expected for current and future CMB surveys, we find that neglecting birefringence produces a positive bias in the lensing bandpowers that increases towards small angular scales. For a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum $L(L+1)C_L^{\alpha\alpha}/2\pi=10^{-5}\,{\rm rad}^2$, the positive fractional bias can reach $(10.1\pm1.1)\%$ of the lensing power at $1375<L<2000$. Jointly estimating lensing and birefringence in the MUSE framework recovers the input lensing bandpowers and birefringence amplitude without detectable bias across all tested configurations. The joint MUSE estimator also reduces the scatter of the recovered birefringence amplitude by factors of $1.6\pm0.2$ to $2.4\pm0.3$ relative to a joint quadratic estimator, with the largest gains in the highest signal-to-noise configurations. These results indicate that a joint-field reconstruction with MUSE can recover unbiased estimates of the lensing and birefringence power spectra while still improving precision relative to quadratic estimators.
comments: 15 pages, 3 figures, prepared for submission to JCAP

figs.cap: When estimating the lensing bandpowers, lensing-only MUSE (open) is biased high by an amount that grows with $A_{\rm CB}^{\rm input}$ and with $L$, while joint MUSE (filled) stays near zero in every bin. Panels (a)–(c) correspond to $A_{\rm CB}^{\rm input}=10^{-4}$, $10^{-5}$, and $4.4\times 10^{-6}$. Points show the mean residual of the lensing bandpowers over 50 simulations relative to the realized input power, with standard errors, for joint (filled) and lensing-only (open) MUSE at $\Delta_{P}=1.4$ (circles) and $2.3\,\mu$K-arcmin (diamonds).

Simultaneously modeling anisotropic birefringence does not degrade the lensing precision at currently allowed levels of birefringence (a), and joint MUSE outperforms the joint QE at all angular scales, by a factor that grows towards high $L$ (b). Top panel (a): The ratio of lensing uncertainties for lensing-only to joint MUSE is consistent with unity. Error bars are bootstrap standard errors from 10,000 paired resamples of the 50 realizations. Bottom panel (b): The ratio of lensing uncertainties for the joint QE to joint MUSE is consistently above unity, and approaches five at high $L$. In both cases, the relative performance is largely unaffected by the assumed noise level or birefringence power. Note this breaks down in (a) for very large birefringence power ($A_{\rm CB}=10^{-4}$), which is not shown. The dashed black lines mark unity. Colors denote different levels of birefringence power $A_{\rm CB}^{\rm input}$, while circles versus diamonds denote the two noise levels $\Delta_{P}=1.4$ and $2.3\,\mu$K-arcmin.

title: Electron processing of glycine: evidence for peptide-forming condensation reactions
authors: A. T. Hopkinson, D. V. Mifsud, P. Herczku, Z. Juhász, B. Sulik, N. J. Mason, N. C. Jones, S. V. Hoffmann, A. Cassidy, L. Hornekær, S. Ioppolo
abstract: The discovery of amino acids on asteroids, including samples returned from asteroid Bennu, and the detection of glycine on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko support the hypothesis that glycine can form in extraterrestrial environments. Laboratory experiments show that glycine can form through both energetic and non-energetic processing of interstellar ice analogues. In the interstellar medium, glycine is exposed to various forms of energetic processing, including cosmic rays and the secondary electrons they generate, which have been shown to produce complex organic molecules, including peptides. This work investigates whether peptide-forming chemistry is a general consequence of energetic processing. Films of glycine and glycine-d3 were grown in two ultrahigh-vacuum chambers and irradiated with 1-2 keV electrons. The irradiated samples were subsequently characterised using infrared spectroscopy, temperature-programmed desorption, and vacuum-ultraviolet spectroscopy. Peptide formation through condensation reactions would produce water as a secondary product, and spectra obtained following irradiation of glycine-d3 showed evidence of D2O formation, supported by TPD measurements, which revealed H2O formation for glycine and H2O, HDO, and D2O for glycine-d3. VUV spectra of irradiated glycine showed the formation of decomposition products, including CO and CO2, as well as H2O. Following heating, a non-volatile residue remained on the surface. Electron irradiation of glycine produces reaction products similar to proton irradiation, suggesting that the resulting chemistry is not strongly dependent on the energy source. These findings support the possibility that larger organic molecules can form in a wide range of extraterrestrial environments. Such molecules may subsequently be incorporated into small bodies and delivered to planetary surfaces, potentially contributing to the emergence of life.
comments: 9 pages, 5 main article figures, 4 appendix figures, to be submitted to A&A

title: Robustness of Transition Probabilities of Spectral Lines Deduced from Spatially Resolved Solar Spectra
authors: Dušan Vukadinović, H. N. Smitha, Andreas Lagg, Sami K. Solanki, Juan Carlos Trelles Arjona
abstract: Atomic parameters are a key ingredient for the synthesis of spectral lines to model observed spectra and to extract meaningful physical information about the observed astrophysical object. We use quiet-sun observations to test the reliability of the atomic parameter inference from observed spectra. Our focus is on the transition probability of spectral lines, denoted as log(gf). We apply a spectropolarimetric inversion method to quiet-sun disc-centre observations at 1.56 $\mu$m from the GRIS/GREGOR spectrograph. We use the coupled method implemented in the globin inversion code, where atomic parameters are spatially coupled, and a single value of these parameters is determined for every spectral line over the entire field of view. We carry out tests to determine the sensitivity of the inferred log(gf) values to various atmospheric parameters and the data reduction fallibility. We find that our log(gf) values are weaker by 0.023 dex compared to the most recent study. This is most probably caused by the constraint imposed on the log(gf) parameter due to the spatial coupling, lifting the degeneracy between temperature and log(gf). We use the Markov chain Monte Carlo method to determine the uncertainty in the inferred log(gf) values. For the strongest lines in the spectral region, the uncertainty in log(gf) is 1-4 %, increasing to 12 % for weaker and blended lines. Our tests suggest that the log(gf) values inferred using the coupled method from globin are robust against any local contamination to the observed line profiles, such as spectral stray light, and return a reliable and unique set of log(gf) values for the strongest lines irrespective of the chosen atmospheric model and observation dataset. This result is valid as long as the underlying assumptions of line formation under local thermodynamic equilibrium and the completeness of the line list are satisfied.
comments: Accepted for publication in A&A; abstract abridged for arxiv; 15 pages

title: The evolution of discs and the epoch of formation of giant planets around low-mass stars
authors: Raffaele Gratton, Elisabetta Rigliaco
abstract: Large-grain depletion in the inner discs of young stellar systems provides a potential observational signature of dust filtration by forming giant-planet cores. In a previous study, we found that $0.50\pm0.10$ of prominent protoplanetary discs around solar-type stars ($0.7$--$1.5$~\Msun) with ages of 2--8~Myr show evidence for a depletion of large grains inside the snow line. Such a depletion may arise when a sufficiently massive planetary core acts as a barrier to the inward drift of large grains, filtering them from the inner disc. If this interpretation is correct, the frequency of dust-filtration signatures should decrease towards lower stellar masses, in accordance with the lower occurrence rate of giant planets around low-mass stars. Extending our analysis to lower-mass stars, we found that only $0.09\pm0.09$ of discs around stars with masses of $0.30$--$0.58$~\Msun, corresponding to the progenitors of main-sequence early M-type stars, show evidence of grain filtration. This fraction is lower than that measured for solar-type stars and is consistent with the lower frequency of giant planets around M-type stars. We also found that discs exhibiting evidence of filtration tend to have relatively massive outer dust reservoirs, with dust masses exceeding $20$~\MEarth. Conversely, the absence of filtration signatures in lower-mass discs suggests that Neptune-mass and lower-mass planets, despite being common around low-mass stars, may generally be unable to filter large grains efficiently.

title: Sulfur chemistry in temperate N$_2$-dominated exoplanetary atmospheres investigated through experimental simulations: Volatile characterization
authors: Louis Maratrat, Adam Yassin Jaziri, Ludovic Vettier, Audrey Chatain, Maeva Millan, Nathalie Carrasco
abstract: Aims. This study addresses through an experimental approach an understudied aspect of sulfur atmospheric chemistry which is the coupled and complex reactivity existing between sulfur, carbon, and nitrogen elements. Experimental simulations have been used to better characterize the volatile products resulting from the coupling between these three elements and discuss the potential observability of such species. Sulfur chemistry appears as a source of diversified signatures which need to be characterized for the current and the future exploration of exoplanetary atmospheres. Methods. SO$_2$ and H$_2$S reactivity was explored experimentally in plasma discharges using mixtures of either pure N$_2$ or composed of N$_2$ and CH$_4$. The volatile species produced in such conditions were analyzed and quantified by in situ mass spectrometry. Results. SO$_2$ reactivity in the presence of N$_2$ alone or combined with methane led to the detection of six sulfur species: H$_2$S, NHSO, S$_2$O, CS$_2$, OCS, and CH$_3$SH. Under the same conditions, the reactivity of H$_2$S resulted in the observation of CS$_2$, CS, and CH$_3$SH. The detection of these species highlights the need to establish a consistent photochemical network describing this sulfur chemistry. Furthermore, the study addresses the detectability of these sulfur compounds via transit spectroscopy. Among them, OCS and CS$_2$, exhibit several detectable bands in the mid-infrared, and constitute promising targets to probe sulfur active chemistry with space- telescopes. In contrast, the detection of the other sulfur volatiles observed appears more challenging at low spectral resolution.
comments: Accept

title: The 2026 iron meteorite fall near Zadzim (Poland) and atmospheric ablation of iron meteoroids
authors: Jiri Borovicka, Pavel Spurny, Lukas Shrbeny, Mateusz Zmija
abstract: Understanding the process of penetration of cosmic material through the Earth's atmosphere is important for linking the atmospheric and ground effects with the properties of original bodies. It has been shown previously that the main process affecting the fate of stony impactors is atmospheric fragmentation. Much less is known about iron impactors,mainly because the scarcity of data about actual iron meteorite falls. Here we present the trajectory, dynamics, light curve, spectrum, and orbit of a fireball which occurred on April 17, 2026, over Poland and was observed by the European Fireball Network and the Skytinel Network. Based on the fireball observations, single 2.9 kg iron meteorite was recovered in the municipality of Zadzim. Analysis of the fireball data revealed no fragmentation although the body suffered a relatively large dynamic pressure of 5.2 MPa. Fitting the light curve needed luminous efficiency 3 times larger than for stony meteoroids. The initial mass was about 19 kg, corresponding to an effective size of 17 cm. We fitted the light curves of 7 other fireballs produced by iron meteoroids with sizes of 2.5 - 13 cm. The ablation coefficient reached enormously high values of about 1 kg/MJ in small meteoroids causing the material to be exhausted and the fireball to end suddenly high in the atmosphere. In the present case, the value did not exceed 0.08 kg/MJ and relaxed to 0.023 kg/MJ towards the end, enabling part of the meteoroid to survive as meteorite. We conclude that the fate of iron meteoroids strongly depends on their size. The reason probably is the high thermal conductivity of iron which leads to complete overheating and easy melting of smaller meteoroids. The orbits of 44 iron fireballs are also provided.
comments: accepted in A&A

title: Assessing the total mass of the Planck protocluster candidates with CMB lensing stacking
authors: Tanguy Dusserre, Hervé Dole, Mathieu Langer, Giulio Fabbian
abstract: Galaxy clusters in formation, or protoclusters, are important sites regarding the evolution of large scale structures and the star formation history of the Universe. With a few exceptions, only their member galaxies have been routinely observed so far. The majority of their mass is expected to be under the form of non baryonic dark matter and cold intergalactic gas. The Planck high redshift star-forming field sample compiles 2151 protocluster candidates, among which 1012 fall within the footprint of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). The lensing of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) by foreground structures allows us to try and assess the total mass of these protoclusters for the first time. We stack the CMB lensing data from ACT at the location of the Planck protocluster candidates to obtain a mean convergence signal. We then provide an estimate for the mean mass along the line of sight for these objects. The centre of the stacked field corresponds to a lensing signal at a $12\,\sigma$ significance level. The integration of the mass along the line of sight yields a value of $(6.6\pm 1.4) \times 10^{14}\,M_\odot$, similar to what is expected from numerical simulations. With the constraint $1.5 < z < 3$ from Planck, we are able to rule out the possibility that this sample is populated by virialised massive structures. This is the first time that the mass of Planck high redshift sources is measured in such a direct way. The results we obtain constitute a new strong argument in favour of this sample being composed of a majority of galaxy protoclusters lying at $z \geq 1$.

title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
authors: Masahiro Hoshino, Shuichi Matsukiyo, Takanobu Amano
abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.
comments: accepted for publication in Physics of Plasmas

title: Photometric Characterisation and Evolutionary State Investigation of the Low Mass-Ratio Contact Binary FASTT 1558
authors: Anurag Baruah, Mayukh Pahari, Kumar Pranshu, Nihal Mohamed Thalakkott, Kuntal Misra, Ikyatha Tummalapalli
abstract: Contact binaries with low mass ratios, as potential progenitors of stellar mergers, offer important insights into the physical processes governing mass and energy transfer. In this work, we present the first spectro-photometry based evolutionary investigation of FASTT 1558, a totally eclipsing, low mass-ratio contact binary. We combine TESS and ASAS-SN photometry with phase-resolved spectroscopy obtained with the 3.6m Devasthal Optical Telescope. The lightcurve modeling with PHOEBE shows that the system has an exceptionally low secondary-to-primary mass ratio of $q=0.1544\pm0.0013$, with a deep contact degree of $f=0.61\pm0.01$. Our analysis yields a total system mass of $1.92\pm0.31\,M_\odot$, while the distance to the system is estimated to be $648.45\pm29.85$ pc. Analysis of long-term eclipse timings reveals an apparent orbital period decrease of $\dot{P}=-(3.03\pm0.26) \times 10^{-7}$ ${\rm day\,yr^{-1}}$, which may be associated with mass-transfer from the primary to the secondary on a thermal timescale. The spectra show phase-dependent H$\alpha$ and CaII equivalent widths, indicating a dynamically evolving chromosphere. Binary evolution calculations with MESA terminates through L2 overflow before reaching the observed low mass-ratio. Despite its extreme mass ratio, the system is presently Darwin stable, with $J_{\rm spin}/J_{\rm orb}=0.15\pm0.02$. FASTT 1558 therefore provides a robust observational benchmark for evolutionary models of low mass-ratio contact binaries.
comments: 24 pages, 13 figures, 9 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ

title: Kepler-404: A near-resonant pair of sub-Neptunes. Reinterpreting a false-positive signal with the novel detection method RIVERS.radon
authors: Yannick Eyholzer, Marylyn Rosenqvist, Adrien Leleu, Vitaliy Kinakh, Slava Voloshynovskiy
abstract: According to the current understanding of planet formation and evolution, (near)-resonant systems should be a common occurrence in nature. However, pairs of planets with period ratios close to commensurability are rarely observed. In this paper, we discuss how observational bias caused by transit timing variations (TTVs) can affect the detection of low signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) planets in transit surveys, playing a role in the lack of representation of these systems. We present an alternative detection method, this http URL, which overcomes the effect of TTVs on planet detectability by not relying on an exact periodic solution for the transit signal. It leverages 2D representations of the light curve and approximates the transits with a set of local periodic solutions with the use of 2D cross-correlation. We present an application of this http URL to the near-resonant system Kepler-404, showing that the signal of the false-positive candidate KOI-2768.03 belongs to the planet Kepler-404b and that it is in a near 5:4 resonance with its companion Kepler-404c, causing TTVs of amplitudes 117.64 and 110.09 minutes, respectively. With a photodynamical fit, we retrieve a pair of similar planets, respectively of radii $1.68^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$ and $1.69^{+0.10}_{-0.10}\,R_\oplus$ and of masses $1.91^{+0.41}_{-0.33}$ and $2.34^{+0.47}_{-0.40}\,M_\oplus$. We find that these planets exhibit typical (near)-resonant features: their densities are lower than the bulk population of exoplanets, and their orbits are nearly coplanar. Interestingly, the planets are found outside the resonance but at a significant distance from the equilibrium point of the $(X_{\rm res}, \delta)$ plane of the Hamiltonian, which is consistent with post-disk instability but somewhat at odds with the observed coplanarity.
comments: 14 pages, 11 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A

title: The ALMA REBELS Survey: multi-band dust continuum observations reveal heavily obscured starbursts among UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$
authors: Hiddo Algera, Lucy Astles, Hanae Inami, Manuel Aravena, Tom Bakx, Rychard Bouwens, Rebecca Bowler, Karin Cescon, Chian-Chou Chen, Elisabete da Cunha, Claudia Di Cesare, Andreas Faisst, Andrea Ferrara, Rebecca Fisher, Yoshinobu Fudamoto, Luca Graziani, Ikki Mitsuhashi, Shoichiro Mizukoshi, Themiya Nanayakkara, Katherine Ormerod, Lucie Rowland, Raffaella Schneider, Sander Schouws, Renske Smit, Laura Sommovigo, Mauro Stefanon, Aswin Vijayan, Paul van der Werf, Joris Witstok
abstract: Detailed studies with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) have shown that dust is widespread even in UV-luminous galaxies at $z\gtrsim6.5$. Multi-band continuum observations are critical to fully characterize these early dust reservoirs. We present a homogeneous analysis of multi-band ALMA observations from the REBELS Large Program and seven follow-up programs, targeting thirteen massive galaxies at $6.5\lesssim z\lesssim7.7$ in at least two bands, including Band 8. Through optically thin modified blackbody fitting, we infer the dust masses, temperatures, and infrared luminosities of our targets. Their dust temperatures span $T_\mathrm{dust}\approx30-70\,\mathrm{K}$, and a stack reveals an average $T_\mathrm{dust}=49_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{K}$. Three sources nominally qualify as ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs; $L_\mathrm{IR}>10^{12}\,L_\odot$), with total star formation rates of $\mathrm{SFR}_\mathrm{UV+IR}\approx160-300\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the highest of which is found in our most distant target, REBELS-18 at $z=7.67$. Their star formation is heavily obscured, with $\gtrsim90\%$ emerging in the infrared, compared to an already large average obscured fraction of $f_\mathrm{obs}=0.75\pm0.11$ for the stack. These SFRs are consistent with the reconstructed growth histories of some massive quiescent galaxies at $z\approx4-5$, suggesting that dusty yet UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$ are plausible progenitors of such systems. The sample moreover displays large dust-to-stellar mass ratios ($M_\mathrm{dust}/M_\star = 0.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}\%$), best reproduced by models in which dust grows efficiently in the interstellar medium. This demonstrates that a dust-rich, IR-luminous, and heavily obscured galaxy population is already in place well into the Epoch of Reionization.
comments: 27 pages + appendices; 15 figures in main text; to be submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics

The dual-band stack reveals a typical $T_{\mathrm{dust}}\approx 50\,\mathrm{K}$.

The cosmic evolution of dust temperatures from $\mathbf{z=0-8.3}$. Our $z\sim 7$ targets (orange) show a variety of dust temperatures spanning $T_{\mathrm{dust}}\approx 30-70\,\mathrm{K}$ given an assumed $\beta_{\mathrm{IR}}=2.0$, with an average (stacked) $T_{\mathrm{dust}}\approx 50\,\mathrm{K}$ (yellow star). These temperatures are similar to those inferred for LBGs at $z\sim 5-8$ (open circles with thick black outline; DSFGs at $z\gtrsim 6$ are shown with thin grey outlines). A linear fit in $1/T_{\mathrm{dust}}$ to all $z\gtrsim 5$ LBGs is shown in blue, but does not reveal clear evidence for an increase in their typical dust temperatures with redshift. Also overplotted are lower-redshift star-forming galaxies (Schreiber et al., 2018) and SPT-selected DSFGs (Reuter et al., 2020), though we caveat that the latter are generally more IR-luminous than our targets. We moreover show several empirical (Schreiber et al., 2018; Viero et al., 2022) and theoretical (Liang et al., 2019; Sommovigo et al., 2022; Parente et al., 2026, dustyGadget) relations, as well as an LBG stack from Mitsuhashi et al. (2024a, red diamond). Two $z>7$ literature LBGs with particularly well-constrained dust SEDs suggesting hot dust are highlighted (Bakx et al., 2025; Rajulal et al., 2026).

REBELS galaxies have star formation rates consistent with the reconstructed growth tracks of some high-redshift quiescent galaxies. We plot the total (UV+IR) star formation rates of our targets (orange) and literature galaxies with multi-band far-infrared data (grey/black circles) as a function of redshift. The stack (yellow star) has a typical star formation rate of $\mathrm{SFR}=81_{-25}^{+61}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ while some of the REBELS galaxies with warm dust reach considerably higher values (e.g., $\mathrm{SFR}\sim 300\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ for REBELS-18 at $z=7.67$). The growth tracks of various individual quiescent galaxies (Carnall et al., 2023; Glazebrook et al., 2024; de Graaff et al., 2025; Weibel et al., 2025) and a stack of $z\approx 4-5$ QGs (Xiao et al., 2026) are overlaid. We also overplot the rising SFH inferred for the REBELS-IFU targets from Fisher et al. (2026) based on NIRSpec IFU data. REBELS galaxies have SFRs at $z\approx 6.5-8$ similar to those of the reconstructed QG star formation histories, suggesting that (a subset of) them are plausible progenitors of this quiescent population.

Dust-detected, UV-bright Lyman break galaxies at $z\approx 7$ show an average dust-to-stellar mass ratio of $\mathbf{M_{\mathrm{dust}}/M_{\star}\approx 0.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}\%}$. The dust-to-stellar mass ratio is plotted against stellar mass for $z\gtrsim 5$ dusty galaxies, $1\lesssim z\lesssim 4$ DSFGs (Donevski et al., 2020), and compared against model tracks from hydrodynamical simulations (Di Cesare et al., 2023; Choban et al., 2025; Vijayan et al., 2026) and semi-analytical models (Popping et al., 2017b; Vijayan et al., 2019; Dayal et al., 2022). For comparison, we also plot the local relation from Paspaliaris et al. (2026, red dashed line and shading). Taken at face value, dust-to-stellar mass ratios of the REBELS sample are best reproduced by theoretical models in which ISM grain growth is efficient.

title: A homogeneous mass campaign of transiting sub-Neptunes around FGK stars
authors: Pierrot Lamontagne, Rafael Luque, Pedro Figueira, Carlos Cifuentes, Matthew C. Nixon, Luis Welbanks, Enric Pallé, Ilaria Carleo, María Rosa Zapatero Osorio, Dawid Jankowski, Grzegorz Nowak, Natalie M. Batalha, Joseph M. Akana Murphy, Gaia Lacedelli, Felipe Murgas
abstract: Sub-Neptunes are among the most common planets in our Galaxy, but are still poorly understood. Addressing their origins and compositions requires precise bulk densities, but literature values come from studies using different radial velocity (RV) extraction methods, stellar activity treatments, and statistical frameworks, which introduces systematic biases that can lead to spurious conclusions in population-level analyses. We conducted a systematic and homogeneous mass-measurement campaign for 12 sub-Neptune systems observed by Kepler and K2, selected for their absent or poorly constrained masses ($\sigma_{M_p}/M_p > 25\%$). Using new HIRES, HARPS-N, and ESPRESSO spectroscopy as well as archival data, we applied a unified hierarchical Bayesian framework with homogeneous data curation. For HARPS-N and ESPRESSO, we applied four independent extraction pipelines (CCF, SERVAL, LBL, sBART) and combined the posteriors via leave-one-out cross-validation stacking, so that no mass would hinge on a single pipeline. A preferred noise model for each target was selected through a uniform Bayesian procedure. We obtained $>3\sigma$ masses for four transiting planets: Kepler-21 b ($5.66^{+0.65}_{-0.96} M_\oplus$, $7.61^{+0.96}_{-1.28}$ g cm$^{-3}$), K2-66 b ($17.9 \pm 3.2 M_\oplus$, $4.69 \pm 1.31$ g cm$^{-3}$), Kepler-538 b ($10.8^{+2.4}_{-2.8} M_\oplus$), and K2-182 b ($20.1^{+4.5}_{-7.8} M_\oplus$). We also provide updated masses for the non-transiting giants Kepler-65 e and Kepler-129 d, and upper limits for the remaining 15 signals, including the first constraints for K2-184, K2-244, and K2-269. No new non-transiting companion was detected in any system. The semi-amplitudes of the four reductions span a median of $0.75\sigma$ of the stacked posterior, and up to $2.7\sigma$, a systematic that a single-pipeline analysis would ignore.
comments: 17 pages, 8 figures, 6 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (article aa62289-26)

title: Resolving the Hubble Tension at $0.1σ$ with Early Dark Energy: Key Role of the Highest-redshift Galaxies from JWST Observations
authors: Guo-Hong Du, Tian-Nuo Li, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang
abstract: We show that the Hubble tension can be resolved at the $0.1\sigma$ level within the early dark energy (EDE) framework, with the highest-redshift galaxies from the JWST observations playing a key role. By accounting for the reference cosmologies of the JWST ultraviolet luminosity function measurements and combining them with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and DESI baryon acoustic oscillation data, we obtain $H_0=72.76\pm1.00~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ in the axion EDE model, in excellent agreement with SH0ES at the $0.1\sigma$ level. We find that the enhanced galaxy abundances at $z=11$ and $12.5$ play a key role in driving this result. These observations favor stronger small-scale matter power, which can be accommodated by increasing the primordial scalar spectral index $n_{\rm s}$. Under the CMB constraints, the positive correlations among $n_{\rm s}$, $f_{\rm EDE}$, and $H_0$ lead to a higher inferred $H_0$. Allowing additional scale dependence in the primordial power spectrum through $\alpha_{\rm s}$ yields a positive running at more than $4\sigma$, further increasing $H_0$ to $73.75\pm1.04~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with its value even exceeding the SH0ES measurement. These results reveal how high-redshift small-scale structure observations influence the inferred $H_0$ through the interplay between the primordial power spectrum and EDE parameter degeneracies.
comments: 9 pages, 4 figures, 1 table

title: The dust attenuation scaling relation in the TNG50 simulation
authors: Pedro Cataldi, XianZhong Zheng, Antonios Katsianis, Sebastian Schulz, Man Qiao, Jianbo Qin, Zongfei Lyu
abstract: The infrared excess (IRX = L_IR / L_UV) of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) follows a tight scaling relation with star formation rate, gas-phase metallicity, and size up to z ~ 3, providing a key benchmark for galaxy formation models. We test whether TNG50 SFGs, post-processed with the radiative transfer code SKIRT, reproduce the universal IRX relation - linking IRX to metallicity, infrared luminosity, size, and inclination - and identify the origin of any offsets. We analyse 7280 TNG50-SFGs across 0 <= z <= 4, comparing their predicted IRX relations with observations and the EAGLE simulation. We test different dust-to-metal (DTM) ratios and dust compositions, recalibrate galaxy properties to observed scaling relations, and decompose the offsets into individual parameter contributions. TNG50-SFGs match the universal IRX relation closely at 0.5 <= z <= 1, but lie above it at z = 0 (+0.5 dex) and below it at z >= 2 (-0.25 dex). They follow a relation of the same functional form, with a shallower, metallicity-independent L_IR slope. At z ~ 0, TNG50-SFGs are ~1 dex fainter in L_IR than the local calibration sample, requiring extrapolation; at fixed stellar mass and L_IR, simulated and observed IRX agree within 0.04 dex. At z >= 2, TNG50-SFGs are less obscured than predicted, an offset largely removed by lowering their metallicities by ~0.2 dex. Varying the DTM ratio and dust type shifts the offset normalisation without resolving its redshift evolution: a redshift-dependent DTM ratio helps at high z, but not at z = 0. Resolving the low-z discrepancy requires both improved dust models and observational constraints on IR-faint galaxies.

title: The Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) Survey I: Photometric Calibration of NB395 and Metallicity Estimation
authors: Bowen Huang, Nozomu Tominaga, Masashi Chiba, Haibo Yuan, Kai Xiao, Yutaka Komiyama, Miho N. Ishigaki, Rosemary F. G. Wyse, Evan N. Kirby, Carrie Filion, Kohei Hayashi, Tomoaki Ishiyama, Mikito Tanaka, Hajime Susa, L{á}szl{ó} Dobos, Alexander S. Szalay, Tam{á}s Budav{á}ri, Viska Wei, Itsuki Ogami, Yoshihisa Suzuki
abstract: We present the first results of the Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) survey, a narrow-band photometric survey targeting metallicity-sensitive narrow bands using the Hyper Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope. This paper outlines the scientific goals, survey strategy, current observational status, photometric calibration, and metallicity estimation. The current ZERO footprint comprises 21 pointings, covering approximately 35 deg$^2$ along the celestial equator in the NB395 band, reaching NB395 $\sim$ 24.5 mag (10$\sigma$) in one hour, significantly deeper than typical comparable narrow-band Ca H\&K surveys. The NB395 photometry is calibrated using corrected Gaia BP/RP spectra and the recalibrated SDSS Stripe 82 catalog, achieving a typical zero-point precision of $\sim$0.3 per cent and flat-field precision better than 1 per cent on spatial scales larger than 8$^\prime$. Under typical conditions (three repeats; total exposure time $\sim$1 hour), the photometric precision reaches $\sim$1.1 per cent at NB395 $\approx$ 12, $\sim$1.5 per cent at 20, and $\sim$10 per cent at 24. We estimate [Ca/H] using a Physics-constrained Stellar Locus Fitting Method. The resulting [Ca/H] precision is better than 0.18 dex for sources brighter than NB395 $\sim$ 20, spanning a wide metallicity range from metal-rich to the very metal-poor regime ($-3 \le$ [Ca/H]$\le +0.5$). We further show that NB395 traces [Ca/H] more directly than [Fe/H]. The final catalog contains one million sources with NB395 photometry, including 379,216 repeatedly observed and 61,845 with [Ca/H] estimates. These results provide a solid foundation for future ZERO survey, including photometric calibration, stellar parameter determination, and investigations of Galactic structure and chemical evolution.
comments: ApJS in Press

title: A catalog of Gaia DR3 luminous blue variables and candidate luminous blue variables
authors: Maria Messineo, Donald F. Figer
abstract: Galactic LBVs are rare, evolved massive stars whose defining evidence is long-term spectroscopic and photometric instability, including S Doradus-type cycles, and, in exceptional cases, giant eruptions. Candidate LBVs (cLBVs) share LBV-like spectra and/or circumstellar nebulae; however, they lack long-term observational datasets that would detect their long-term variability and confirm their classification as bona fide LBVs. Modern time-domain surveys provide homogeneous light curves for many Galactic massive stars, but each survey has its own limitations in terms of depth, temporal coverage, and observing cadence. Using confirmed Galactic LBVs as a control sample, we aim to test what Gaia DR3 and complementary photometric surveys can and cannot establish about LBV-type variability. We assembled a vetted sample of 75 Galactic LBVs and cLBVs with near- and mid-infrared photometry from 2MASS, MSX, WISE, GLIMPSE, and MIPSGAL. The infrared material was used to validate identifications, evaluate source confusion, and place objects in a circumstellar-dust context. We then constructed light curves from Gaia DR3, the Bochum survey, the ASAS SN, and the ZTF, and analyzed large-amplitude and periodic cases with Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods. Gaia DR3 matches are available for 67% of the sample and 76% are reported as variable. We identify high-amplitude variables and periodic systems that may be binaries rather than classical LBVs. Six confirmed LBVs and five candidates show variations larger than 0.6 mag in the Gaia RP filter. Their light curves are examined and three periodic variables are identified. The light curves of OMN2000 LS1 and DWC2011 140 show primary and secondary minima, strongly suggesting eclipsing binary systems. OMN2000 LS1 has a well-constrained period of 80.29 d, and DWC2011 140 of 95.07 d.
comments: 18 pages, 11 figures

title: Critical Eddington luminosity and photon cooling of compact spherical stars
authors: Tisha Desai, Jiří Horák, Włodek Kluźniak, Sukalpa Kundu
abstract: Context. Relativistic corrections to the luminosity have been used for neutron stars of radius greater than $3MG/c^2$ in studies of X-ray bursts. However, there is no fundamental limit that excludes the existence of more compact massive objects with a physical surface, fluid or solid. Aims. We aim to discuss critical "Eddington" luminosity for spherical stars that have a surface within the sphere of unstable circular photon orbits (photon sphere). Methods. We use standard analytical ray-tracing formulae in the Schwarzschild metric. Results. We find that for stars within the photon sphere, the Eddington condition for balance between radiative force and gravitational attraction is fundamentally altered by photons returning to the surface. The equilibrium is non-local and requires stationarity on timescales of photon fall-back. As a result, spontaneous symmetry breaking is possible, leading to non-uniformity of emission across the photospheric surface. Conclusions. For a fixed intrinsic luminosity, the photons returning to the surface decrease the cooling rate of stars inside their photon sphere. At the same time, the returning photons increase the value of the critical luminosity that would balance gravity. One and the same redshifted formula applies to the critical luminosity, as seen by a distant observer, for any radius of the star. In the X-ray burst literature, for stars with radius less than 3 gravitational radii a different formula has long been accepted that missed the essential physics of the photons emitted in directions outside the escape cone.
comments: submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics

figs.cap: The ratio of the observed luminosity to the surface luminosity is shown as a function of stellar radius. The ratio tends to zero at the Schwarzschild radius $R=2M$, and gradually increases as the stellar radius becomes larger and the gravitational redshift $(1-2M/R)$ becomes smaller, tending to the Newtonian limit of unity at $R\rightarrow\infty$. However, when the surface of the star is below the photon sphere (gray vertical line at $R_{\rm ph}=3M$), the observed luminosity experiences an additional suppression. The gray dashed line shows the ratio obtained when the effect of the escape cone is ignored.

The critical luminosity required to balance gravity is increased owing to the force exerted by the returning photons (fallback) when the stellar surface lies below the photon sphere, located at radius $R=3M$ shown in the gray vertical line.

The ratio of the observed emission at critical luminosity to the ordinary Eddington luminosity is plotted as a function of the stellar radius, solid line, Eq. (20). In the X-ray burst literature it has been assumed that the ratio would be suppressed (as shown in the dashed line) owing to the presence of the escape cone when the stellar surface lies below the photon sphere. However, we show that this effect will be compensated by an increase in the critical luminosity required to balance the gravitational force.
The critical luminosity required to balance the gravitational forces at the photosphere (abscissa) and its value observed at infinity (ordinate).

Compactness of the star vs. the observed luminosity, Eq. (27), in units of mass accretion rate, $L_{\infty}/(\dot{M}c^{2})$, in the case where accretion occurs from the ISCO. title: Constraining the Binary Fraction and Mass-Ratio Distribution of FGK Dwarfs with Gaia XP Spectra: Metallicity, $α$-Element, and Age Dependencies
authors: Yinuo Zhang, Zexi Niu, Haibo Yuan, Ning-Chen Sun, Jia-Hui Wang, César Rojas-Bravo, Jifeng Liu
abstract: We present a study of the binary fraction and mass-ratio distribution for near 200,000 FGK dwarf stars within 1 kpc, utilizing the Stellar Locus Outlier (SLOT) method applied to synthetic Gaia XP photometry and stellar parameters from LAMOST DR9. By modeling the asymmetric color residuals relative to a metallicity-dependent single-star locus, we measure the binary fraction $f_b$ and constrain the power-law slope $\gamma_{\rm large\,q}$ of the mass-ratio distribution at high mass ratio $q$. Higher metallicity is associated with a steeper (more negative) $\gamma_{{\rm large}q}$, indicating a larger proportion of low-mass-ratio systems. For $\alpha$-elements, [Mg/H] and [Si/H] are anticorrelated with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples; conversely, [Ca/H] shows a positive correlation with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples. No correlation is found between $f_b$ and $\alpha$-element abundances in thick-disk-dominated subsamples. The binary fraction increases modestly toward older ages in the thin-disk population, a trend that likely reflects underlying correlations with chemistry. Our results shed light on how chemical composition and dynamical processes shape the binary properties of solar-type stars.

title: Off-axis performance characterization of hard X-ray optics for the FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 sounding rocket missions
authors: Yusuke Yoshida, Kazuki Ampuku, Koki Sakuta, Makoto Yoshihara, Keitoku Yoshihira, Ryoma Tanaka, Tetsuo Kano, Naoki Ishida, Wataru Kato, Yoshitaka Inoue, Keisuke Tamura, Takashi Okajima, Kikuko Miyata, Noriyuki Narukage, Gota Yamaguchih, Hidekazu Takano, Yoshiki Kohmura, Shutaro Mohri, Satoru Egawa, Hiroto Motoyamai, Takehiro Kume, Yusuke Matsuzawa, Yoichi Imamura, Takahiro Saito, Kentaro Hiraguri, Hirokazu Hashizume, Hidekazu Mimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi
abstract: FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 are Japan--U.S. joint sounding rocket missions investigating particle acceleration and plasma heating in solar flares. We developed soft and hard X-ray optics for both missions and characterized the off-axis response of the hard X-ray optics. Imaging performance was measured at SPring-8 BL29XUL, and effective areas at NASA/GSFC. With increasing off-axis angle, focused images became elongated and the large-angle component of the point spread function increased. The Half Power Diameter (HPD) remained below 20 arcsec up to 7.5 arcmin, increasing to approximately 50 arcsec at 15 arcmin. A Wolter-I optics model reproduced the off-axis HPD dependence within approximately 20%, with residuals likely associated with azimuthal variations in mirror figure errors. On-axis effective areas were 41.3 +/- 1.9 mm^2 at 6.4 keV and 32.3 +/- 1.6 mm^2 at 10 keV, decreasing by 20% and 30%, respectively, at 5 arcmin. Incorporating an empirical correction for geometric effects and X-ray reflectivity reproduced measured effective areas within 20% over 1.0--12.5 keV up to 5 arcmin. At larger off-axis angles, deviations at lower energies suggest increasing stray-light contributions. These measurements provide off-axis response data for constructing response functions for FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 analyses.

title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
authors: Timur Dzhatdoev, Ilya Kudryashov, Anatoly Semenov
abstract: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. We consider two basic scenarios of CR origin: I) the supergalactic scenario assuming diffusion of the protons inside a magnetic field structure with the characteristic radius $H = 1-20$ Mpc and II. the cosmological scenario with the maximum redshift of the sources $z_{max} = 6$.
comments: 3 pages, 1 figure

title: Stellar-evolution systematic biases on $^{12}\text{C}(α,γ)^{16}\text{O}$ constraints from the primordial-black-hole mass gap
authors: Jiancheng Wang, Xiaogu Zhong, Jirong Mao
abstract: The $^{12}\text{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\text{O}$ reaction determines helium-burning carbon-oxygen core masses and sets the pair-instability-supernova mass-gap boundary, which limits the maximum mass of stellar-origin primordial black holes. Gravitational-wave population analyses using GWTC-4 report a low-spin-black-hole upper cutoff at $68.5^{+19.8}_{-18.5}\,M_\odot$, implying a low astrophysical S-factor $S_{300}\approx 108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$, in tension with canonical nuclear-astrophysics evaluations. However, stellar-evolution systematic uncertainties from metallicity, rotation, and mass-loss prescriptions remain poorly quantified. Here we use the MESA stellar-evolution code to construct a three-dimensional parameter grid disentangling these coupled effects. We show that metallicity-dependent winds dominate helium-core retention; rotation suppresses carbon consumption via centrifugal cooling and meridional mixing; different mass-loss prescriptions produce $8$-$10\,M_\odot$ offsets in the black-hole-mass-gap edge. A parameter combination $Z\approx10^{-3}$, moderate rotation $\omega/\omega_\mathrm{crit}=0.4$, and optically-thin C15 winds reproduces the GWTC-4 inferred maximum primordial-black-hole mass for $S_{300}=108.6\,\mathrm{keV\,barn}$. The canonical $45\,M_\odot$ gap boundary represents an overlapping statistical intersection of black-hole-population distributions rather than a universal physical threshold. Our framework provides a pathway to jointly constrain nuclear-reaction rates, stellar-evolution physics, and gravitational-wave-source populations.
comments: 5 pages, 6 figures, Accepted by MNRAS

title: The W Transform: an additional powerful tool for astrophysical time-series analysis
authors: P. D. S. de Lima, D. O. Fontinele, R. L. Gomes, B. L. Canto Martins, J. M. de Araújo, Y. Wang, J. R. De Medeiros, I. C. Leão
abstract: This work introduces the W Transform (WT) for astrophysical applications and explores its similarities and differences to the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), in photometric stellar light curves (LCs). We tested both techniques on synthetic data, producing LCs with different noise levels and numbers of gaps, and applied them to LCs from TESS space mission. The analysis focused on six stars: the solar analog TIC 276293046, the ultra-cool dwarf TIC 359892714, the $\gamma$ Dor pulsator TIC 164173105, the eclipsing binary TIC 355151781, the hosting planet star TIC 142276270, and the brown dwarf TIC 102076870. Overall, the results were in agreement, except for stars with LCs presenting sector-to-sector differences in structures or changes in the number of gaps, reflecting time-dynamic effects in the same target, which affect how time-dependent variability features appear in the time-frequency representation. For such LCs, the WT spectra are more stable and accurate in recovering signal amplitudes than the CWT maps, which exhibit distortions and limitations, showing that the inherent flexibility of the WT method in adjusting the dominant frequency could enhance time resolution even in LCs with complex or variable structures. We conclude that the WT is a robust tool for the analysis of stellar LCs, and that both methods may complement each other in an in-depth analysis of a periodic astrophysical signal. The present results suggest that the WT is a robust and accurate tool for analyzing stellar LCs, expanding the range of numerical techniques available for analyzing different stellar periodic phenomena from photometric observations.

title: TWIN-1: A new 185 to 350 MHz Two-Element Radio Interferometer for Solar Observation at Gauribidanur
authors: Abhishek R, G N Paneendra, Raghavendra Rao K B, Keerthipriya S, Katta Naveen, Anumanchi Agastya Sai Ram Likhit, Arul Pandian B, Vinod K R, Roshan Kumar Dora, Arutkeerthi N, Deep Bhowmik, Krishna Balaji S, Sahana Bhattramakki, Prabu Thiagaraj
abstract: We present details of a new two-element radio interferometer, namely the TWIN, developed for routine monitoring of solar events at the Gauribidanur Observatory (77.428°E, 13.603°N) between 185 MHz and 350 MHz. This interferometer is built using custom-built antennas, an indigenous RF front-end consisting of LNAs, power combiners, and high-gain amplifiers, and RF over fiber signal transport modules. A data capture system was developed using a commercial digital storage oscilloscope and controlled with custom-designed Python-based tools. The oscilloscope digitises the RF signals with a time resolution of 0.8 ns, bursts of 9952 time samples, with a nominal duty cycle of 3 seconds, and the resultant data is collected on a remote computer. Specialised tools were developed to analyse the data and detect solar events. The interferometer has been operational since July 2023. In our analysis, we have detected several solar events from the ongoing Solar Cycle 25. This paper outlines the design philosophy, signal flow, commissioning and validation, results from a solar event, and future plans for data capture, data analysis, and archival.
